accounting.rationale: PDF 79, printed 65, lines 21-26 defines the directional type-compatible relation. Whether a particular operation requires that relation is supplied by its canonical owner, not by a fabricated local rejection rule.

Lines 21-22: a nonpolymorphic entity's compatibility is limited to the same declared type, subject to the following enum exception. Same intrinsic category is not same parameter values; 7.5.2.4 defines derived identity and 7.6 defines the two nonderived identities.
Lines 21-23: the extra route concerns an entity of an enum type, not enumeration type and not every integer-like object. 7.6.1 defines a named enum and integer enumerators.
The exceptional counterpart must be an expression of type integer. An arbitrary different nonintrinsic type or merely convertible representation is not covered.

That integer expression must contain a primary that is an enumerator of this enum type. A numerically equal integer literal, a variable initialized from the enumerator, or an enumerator from a different enum is not interchangeable with this syntactic/semantic premise. The primary need not be the whole expression.
Lines 23-24: a polymorphic entity other than unlimited polymorphic is compatible with entities having its declared type. Its current dynamic type is not substituted for that declared type.

The same entity is also compatible with entities of any extension of its declared type. The transitive and self-extension definitions are 7.5.7.1 p3; the relation is not symmetric. Extensibility excludes SEQUENCE/BIND and the specified intrinsic-module pointer types.

Lines 24-25: an unlimited entity is compatible with all entities despite having no declared type. TYPE(*) and CLASS(*) still have different use restrictions; this compatibility does not waive C714-C716 or 15.5.2.5's assumed-type actual exclusions.

Lines 25-26 lift entity-to-entity compatibility to entity-to-type compatibility by reference to entities of that type. This does not include kind, LEN, rank, coarray, attribute or allocation-state compatibility automatically.
The unnumbered note after p1 illustrates asymmetry with a root and extension. The displayed declarations are schematic, not a standalone conforming program or a new mandatory case.
The note's second derived type extends its first and the example entities have the corresponding named CLASS declarations.
Compatibility from CLASS(root) toward CLASS(extension) follows the named-polymorphic extension definition.
The reverse does not follow: an ancestor is not thereby an extension of its child. Neither SAME_TYPE_AS nor an unqualified EXTENDS_TYPE_OF result is a general compatibility oracle.

PDF 79 lines 27-29 admits compatible types for polymorphic allocation and compatible objects for pointer/dummy association. It does not require a program to exercise every such choice and does not cancel canonical allocation/association restrictions.

Lines 27-28 permit a polymorphic allocatable to be allocated with a compatible type, subject to C937-C951, abstract-type exclusions, kind/length and rank rules. Defined allocation effects are accounted under 7.3.2.3 p5, not duplicated here.

Lines 28-29 permit polymorphic pointer association to compatible objects during execution. C1016/C1017 separately constrain type and kind, C1022 rank, and C1028 eligible targets; 10.2.2.3 adds state and parameter conditions. Compatibility alone is not sufficient for a valid pointer assignment.

Lines 28-29 permit polymorphic dummy association to compatible objects, subject to ordinary versus allocatable/pointer dummy rules in 15.5.2.5-.8, exact kind and applicable length conditions, rank, effective arguments and live allocation/association. In particular 15.5.2.6's same-declared-type requirements cannot be replaced by this broader permission.

review_rationale: Independent source/link review and verified integration: doc/source_audits/batch_008.json. Type compatibility definitions and the informative note are source-accounted without manufactured executable programs or false SAME_TYPE_AS/EXTENDS_TYPE_OF claims.
